title: Enoch and the Watchers
opening_question: Who was Enoch, who were "the sons of God" in Genesis 6, and what does the New Testament say about them?

steps.question: What does Genesis say about Enoch, and what does Hebrews add?
Who took wives in Genesis 6, and who were born? Where else does the Old Testament say "sons of God"?
Jude quotes a prophecy of Enoch. Read it next to 1 Enoch 1:9: what is the same, and what is different?
What do Peter's letters say about spirits in prison and angels that sinned?
What does Jesus say about angels and marriage? Read it as part of the whole counsel.
The Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 6–16, Ethiopian Canon): who came down, what did they teach, and what was their judgement?
Jubilees 4–5 (Ethiopian Canon): what does it say about Jared's days, Enoch, and the angels of God?

remember.text: "Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him"
By faith Enoch was "translated that he should not see death".
Genesis 6 and Job 1 both speak of the "sons of God".
Jude quotes a prophecy of Enoch; 1 Enoch 1:9 has words like it.
Peter writes of the "angels that sinned"; Jesus says in the resurrection they are "as the angels of God in heaven".

quiz.q: Which verse says "Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him"?

options: A priest of the most high God
